newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Phone rates pushed up Argentine Feb inflation-govt.
newsitem.headline: Phone rates pushed up Argentine Feb inflation-govt.

text.p: The rise in Argentina's telephone rates was the main contributor to the 0.4 percent increase in consumer prices in February, the Economy Ministry said.
Of the nine sectors monitored to measure changes in consumer prices, the transport and communications part rose 3.6 percent, by far the largest rise of all the sectors, said the ministry.

A breakdown provided by the ministry showed the communications segment alone rose a massive 58.4 percent in the month, accounting for virtually the whole rise in the transport and communications sector.
Of the other subsets of that sector, public transport was flat, personal transport rose 0.1 percent and vehicle maintenance was up 0.1 percent.
Late in January the government decreed the introduction of a change to Argentina's telephone rates regime.

The changes included the abolition of free local call time, boosted the prices of other local calls and increased monthly rental charges. At the same time, the cost of long-distance domestic calls was cut by 56 percent and international call rates to major destinations were reduced by an average 42 percent.

The other sectors monitored by the government mostly remained flat or fell over the month. Food rose 0.2 percent, clothing fell 0.7 percent, housing rose 0.7 percent, household goods fell 0.1 percent, health was flat, entertainment fell 0.3 percent, education was flat and others were flat.
The ministry announced late Tuesday that consumer prices rose 0.4 percent in February, compared with a 0.3 percent drop a year earlier and a 0.5 percent rise in January this year.
Wholesale prices fell 0.2 percent in February, versus a decrease of 0.1 percent in February 1996 and a 0.2 percent rise in January.
